items.title: v3.4.1 — audit the README against the code, and fix the two lines it caught
items.body:
"Update the readme" was open-ended, so I read it as: audit every claim against what the code actually does, and fix the drift. Six releases had left the body describing an app that no longer exists.

## Seven claims were wrong, not merely stale

| README said | reality |
|---|---|
| "exactly two `fetch(` calls" | **six** — `structure.test.js:110` has asserted six since 3.1.0 |
| "every module except `escape.js` depends on `waffledist`" | **four of eleven** `require` anything at all |
| "`run.js` reports a combined total" | it has never summed assertions |
| "`_assert.js`: three assertions" | two assertions and a reporter |
| "the other 5 are alternates past the line" | four are — the fifth is **Bishopville's own primary**, which carries no *(past the line)* label because the tag is only emitted on alternates |
| honorary row "carries its evidence in `note`" | asserted as a flag **or** a note |
| v3.0.0: "the seven `lib/` modules are untouched" | five lines after that entry says it rewrote the polyline decoder |

## Stale from later releases

The intro's Route bullet, "the one mode that talks to a *routing* API", "no ranking" (route options are now compared), the per-route detour tier (`projectAll` shares one across options), and the theme key now moving the basemap.

## Four sections the body was missing

Map theming, the trip drawer, the address fields and alternative routes existed **only in the changelog** — a reader had to reconstruct current behaviour from release notes. They're body sections now:

- **The map follows the theme, and never overrules the driver** — including why it's an allow-list by identity and how Satellite survives a dusk transition
- **The trip drawer** — the both-ways toggle, the `ResizeObserver`, and why form controls are 16px
- **The pickup and delivery fields** — autosuggest, the debounce as a call-volume decision, and the GPS button's two distinct failure modes
- **Alternative routes** — the scoring, why HERE's ordering is kept, and the shared detour tier

## Two fixes landed in code, not prose

The `HERE calls` comment in `index.html` carried the **same "two GETs" claim** the README did — the README was describing it accurately, and both were wrong.

The filter panel's fine print calls them "the three 'confirmed' filters" while only two of the three toggles said *Confirmed*. The **label** was the inconsistent half, so `fDiner` now reads **Confirmed sit-down diner**. That's the only user-visible change here, and why this is a version bump rather than a docs commit.

## One correction to my own earlier work

`lib/routewaffles.js` claimed the bounding-box reject measured **185ms → 52ms across six routes**. That figure came from the v3.2.0 design and I transcribed it into the comment without re-running it. Re-running my actual benchmark gives **five routes at roughly 150ms → 47ms (~3.1–3.3×)** — which is what the README's v3.2.0 entry already said. The comment now matches what was measured; the README entry was right and stands, with a note that the 507-comparison differential harness was a scratch script and isn't in `test/`.

## Verified

`node test/run.js` — all green, **965 assertions across 12 files**. No duplicate headings, all internal cross-references resolve, and the only remaining mentions of the old wrong claims are inside the v3.4.1 entry describing what was fixed.

`APP_VERSION` 3.4.0 → 3.4.1, all eleven lib stamps moved. `ATLAS_REV` unchanged.

items.title: Restructure top-level README as a reader-first landing page
items.body:
## Summary

Restructures the top-level `README.md` (and its `zh/` mirror) so it works primarily as a reader-facing landing page for the knowledge base rather than a maintainer manual. Reader-facing navigation now precedes repository structure and contribution details. Information architecture only — no taxonomy, work cards, or papers were touched.

### New section order

`Intro` → **Start Exploring** (Browse by Topic / Domain / All Works) → **Browse by Topic** → **Browse by Domain** → **Scope** → **Repository Structure** → **Contributing**

Previously the page led with the directory tree, layer-model prose, and two `filename`-column taxonomy tables; the only reader-facing navigation sat ~90 lines down.

### Key changes

- **Start Exploring** block is now the first actionable section, with the two-axis `Topic → Work → Paper` / `Domain → Work → Paper` diagram.
- **Topic table** uses linked topic names + a "what you'll find" column (drawn from each topic page's own Definition); filename column removed.
- **Domain table** uses linked names grouped **Sciences / Engineering**, sorted by coverage, with a **Works** count column; filename column removed.
- ASCII directory tree replaced by a compact **role table**; layer-model prose compressed and moved below the reading sections.
- **Status** section removed (stale and redundant); its live totals fold into Scope.

### Corrections

- **Card total → 238.** The prior 239 counted `works/README.md` as a card (`ls works/*.md` = 239 files, 238 are cards).
- The old Status section's **per-topic counts were badly stale** (e.g. Scientific Agent Benchmarks shown as 24; actual 156). Rather than add a third drift-prone copy, the homepage now routes topic counts to `topics/README.md`.
- **Domain counts** are included and verified cell-for-cell against `domains/README.md` (exact match on all 19).

### Validation

- All 7 topic links, 19 domain links, and 3 index links resolve; no dead links.
- English and Chinese mirrors kept structurally identical; zh reviewed for natural phrasing.

items.title: The charter: ratified product identity, realigned surfaces, CI-gated job line
items.body:
## What this is

`CHARTER.md` — the one-page ratified contract (problem, user, job, non-goals, invariants, Now/Next/Not-now, done-checks, and the contradictions found with rulings) — built through an operator interview, plus the realignment of every claim-bearing surface to it.

## The ratified identity

- **Problem:** agents break code they can't see, and burn outsized tokens grepping toward understanding.
- **User:** the agent-heavy individual dev on their own repo (CI gate included); team lead secondary.
- **Job line:** **"Your agents break less code and burn fewer tokens."** — now leads the README, site homepage/tagline/og titles, and the npm / plugin / marketplace / MCP-registry / GitHub-About listings.
- **Enforced:** `check-consistency` reads the job line from `CHARTER.md` and fails any of the four listing surfaces that drifts. `CLAUDE.md` (new) points every agent at the charter before product changes.

## Rulings applied in this diff

- **C7 (fabricated premise struck):** the "sponsorship funds the AI bills from benchmarking" story was AI-invented — the benchmarks cost no actual API money. Support copy now says the true thing: sponsoring supports the project, and sponsors get featured README/site placement. Correction banners added to `reports/REVENUE.md` and `docs/proposals/ai-spend-gated.md`.
- **C3:** external review demoted from "Two modes" billing to a feature note; the capability stays.
- **C4:** enterprise support softened to a one-line email doorway — no price, no SLA claim.
- **C1/C5/C6:** `docs/ROADMAP.md` rewritten to the charter's Now/Next/Not-now with dated corrections (program retired as governing plan; measurement stays as the receipts discipline).
- `tests/revenue.test.mjs` realigned: RV2/RV3 now assert the ratified copy and the *absence* of the struck claims.

## Verification

- `npm test`: **918 tests, 0 failures** (870 pass, 48 skipped)
- `npm run check-consistency`: OK — including the new charter job-line check
- `npm run build:site`: docs/ regenerated deterministically

items.title: fix(pipeline): correct QA grader, scorer-agnostic relevancy, honest CODE grading
items.body:
Pipeline-correctness fixes so the scoreboard reflects **actual** benchmark performance. Touches only the eval pipeline (grader/metrics/tests) — **no changes to the team's memory mechanism** (`stores/**`, `okf.py`, `router.py`, `protocols.py`, `claudecode/service.py`, `memory_server.py`, or the BM25 scorer in `harness.py`).

## Changes
- **`eval/memeval/metrics.py`** — correct the QA grader and make **relevancy scorer-agnostic**: relevancy/precision is now derived from the `is_gold` annotation rather than a raw similarity-score threshold, which previously read wildly differently under Jaccard vs BM25 for the same retrieval. Honest CODE grading path.
- **`eval/memeval/agent.py`** — ensure gold annotations are persisted onto the logged trajectory so metrics see them.
- **`eval/tests/test_smoke.py`** — tests covering the corrected grader/relevancy behavior.
- **`results/v0.1/README.md`** — small read-through correction.
- **`suggestion.md`** (new) — memory-improvement suggestions for the team (prose only; not code changes to their mechanism), led by turn-level chunking.

## Validation
Offline smoke suite passes on current main after rebase: `python -m pytest eval/tests/test_smoke.py` → 90 passed, 1 skipped.

## Notes
- BM25 (merged in an earlier PR) is intentionally **kept** — not reverted.
- `suggestion.md` is advisory for the parallel memory work; it makes no changes to the memory mechanism itself.

items.title: docs: reconcile the README Vite and Nuxt benchmark rows with the snapshot
items.body: ## The defect The README table and the generated Blacksmith snapshot published **different numbers for the same two surfaces**, both presented as current: | Surface | `README.md` | `bench/results/tool-benchmark-latest.json` / `performance-blacksmith.md` | | --- | --- | --- | | Vite build | `1.70s` / `1.52s` / **1.1×** | `1.66s` / `732.5ms` / **2.3×** (1,000 files) | | Nuxt build | `6.68s` / `7.35s` / **0.9×** | `6.79s` / `6.42s` / **1.1×** (500 files) | That is not rounding — they are different runs. A reader got a different answer depending on which page they opened, and the README's version was the pessimistic one on both rows. Second, separate problem: the README header asserted > Measured on Blacksmith `blacksmith-32vcpu-ubuntu-2404`, **15,000 generated Vue SFCs**, median of 5 runs as a blanket claim, but only SFC compile, Lint, and Format run at 15,000. From the snapshot's own `surfaces[].files`: Type check **500**, Vite build **1,000**, Nuxt build **500**. The overstatement applied to exactly the three rows that look weakest. ## The change - The **Vite build** and **Nuxt build** rows now come from `bench/results/tool-benchmark-latest.json` — the artifact `docs/content/architecture/performance-blacksmith.md` is rendered from — and the table names that run ([29010164013](https://github.com/ubugeeei-prod/vize/actions/runs/29010164013)) rather than leaving one global link that does not apply to them. - A per-row **Files** column, populated from each surface's own `files` value. - The Nuxt row carries a **pending regeneration** marker. **No number in this PR is invented.** Every cell comes from the committed artifact. Where a fresh measurement is needed, the cell is marked rather than estimated. ## The Nuxt row is marked, not replaced #3409 shows the Nuxt benchmark let `@vizejs/nuxt` inherit a warm persistent pre-compile cache through a `node_modules` symlink shared by every run and both variants — a cache the Nuxt default compiler has no counterpart for. The `1.1×` in the artifact was measured under that harness. **The correction runs against Vize**: the honest cold-vs-cold figure is *worse* than `1.1×`, not better. The row is therefore footnoted as pending a fresh Blacksmith run once #3409 is on `main`. I have not substituted a local estimate, and the local runs I do have are not comparable — my machine was under heavy competing load throughout. ## Scope The **type-check row is deliberately untouched** — it is being retracted separately as an invalid cross-engine ratio (`vue-tsc` is the JavaScript TypeScript compiler, `vize check` is native tsgo). The compile/lint/format rows are from run 29004198781 and are not reconciled here; the table now says so instead of implying one provenance for everything. ## Test `tests/tooling/readme-benchmark-rows.test.ts` — two cases, both `assert.deepEqual` over whole rows so a failure shows the entire expected row: 1. the README's Vite and Nuxt rows equal the rows derived from `bench/results/tool-benchmark-latest.json`, formatted with the same `formatMs` rule the snapshot uses; 2. the header does not assert one corpus size, and every row's Files cell equals that surface's `files` in the artifact. Both **fail on the pre-fix README**, verified by stashing only `README.md`: ``` ✖ the README Vite and Nuxt rows match the committed benchmark snapshot actual: [ undefined, undefined ] expected: [ [ 'Vite build', '1,000', '@vitejs/plugin-vue', '1.66s', '732.5ms', '**2.3×**' ], [ 'Nuxt build', '500', 'Nuxt compiler', '6.79s', '6.42s', '**1.1×**†' ] ] ✖ the README states a per-row corpus size instead of one blanket figure actual: true expected: false ℹ pass 0 ℹ fail 2 ``` and pass after: ``` ✔ the README Vite and Nuxt rows match the committed benchmark snapshot ✔ the README states a per-row corpus size instead of one blanket figure ℹ pass 2 ℹ fail 0 ``` The existing `tests/tooling/readme-boundary.test.ts` still passes (2/2), so the README stays within its size and funnel constraints. ## Gates ``` $ nix develop -c vp run fmt:check # exit 0 $ nix develop -c vp run source:lengths # exit 0 ``` No Rust changed. Should land after #3409. Refs #3363 --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is enabled.

items.title: docs: correct benchmark dataset hierarchy — wiki_all_1M canonical, Cohere legacy (#92 redefined)
items.body:
## Summary

Implements the **redefined** scope of #92 (see the [2026-08-04 redefinition
comment](https://github.com/pg-cuvs/pg_cuvs/issues/92#issuecomment-latest) on
the issue) — the original acceptance ("regenerate the Cohere CSV with
non-zero `index_bytes`") is **withdrawn**. This is documentation/ledger work
only: no GPU, no benchmark reruns, no measured numbers changed.

> 재정의 근거 (issue #92, 2026-08-04): "기준은 이미 wiki_all_1M(cuvs-bench 표준,
> data.rapids.ai)로 옮겨갔다... 대외 커뮤니케이션도 이미 이동했다(2026-07-24 NVIDIA
> 메일은 §2.1b를 인용)... 원래 acceptance는 철회한다 — 해당 결함은 코드 수정
> (#75/#79)으로 이미 해소됐고 그 증거가 wiki1m canonical 산출물이다. 결함 CSV는
> 재측정 대상이 아니라 은퇴 대상이다."

The docs described the project's dataset hierarchy backwards relative to
actual practice: `BENCHMARK.md` declared Cohere 1M×1024 "Primary dataset" and
"canonical" (§2.1a) while carrying a known `index_bytes=0` defect, and
demoted the wiki_all_1M cross-machine reproduction (§2.1b) — the dataset
NVIDIA's 2026-07-24 email and #98 actually cite — to a "reproduction"
footnote.

## Changes (3 commits, split by intent)

1. **Artifact rename + ledger** — `bench/results/pg_cuvsbench_1m.csv` →
   `pg_cuvsbench_1m_legacy.csv` (`git mv`); `bench/results/README.md` ledger
   row updated to `legacy` status with a one-line defect note (was a 17-line
   block); wording states the fix (#75/#79) and canonical wiki_all_1M rows
   as the corrected evidence.
2. **BENCHMARK.md / README.md hierarchy** — §0 "Primary dataset" → wiki_all_1M
   (Cohere relabeled "Legacy dataset"); §2.1a heading/framing: canonical →
   "legacy dataset (Cohere)", scoped as "canonical within the Cohere lineage"
   where that's still accurate (it's the fix lineage for the k-wiring/
   VRAM-accounting defects); §2.1b promoted to canonical. README's benchmark
   section now leads with the wiki_all_1M ~5.4× citation (existing §2.1b
   number, not a new measurement) and demotes the Cohere table to a labeled
   legacy comparison — its own ratios (~4.5× search, ~2× build) are **not
   deleted**, just relabeled per dataset.
3. **Reference sweep** — every live doc naming the old filename or implying
   Cohere-as-primary: `ROADMAP.md` (#92 release-readiness row rewritten for
   the redefined scope; the dated ADR-080 completion entry gets its filename
   updated in place, narrative untouched), `bench/cuvs_bench_backend/README.md`
   + `run_pg_cuvsbench.py` (usage examples), `design/benchmarks/crossover-methodology.md`
   (filename + rename pointer in an existing baseline-reconciliation note).

## What I deliberately did NOT touch

- **`design/specs/phase-record.md:1201`** — `docs/doc-map.md` states it is
  frozen history ("Do not reopen ... it is frozen history"). Left as-is; it
  still names the old filename in a historical evidence line, which is
  accurate as written (it was true at the time).
- **`design/decisions.md` ADR-080 body** (evidence table, numbers, `데이터
  정합성 정정` note) — append-only per `docs/doc-map.md`. Added a short dated
  addendum after the existing block, matching the doc's own precedent for
  self-correction notes (the existing 정정 note at the same ADR), recording
  the hierarchy change without rewriting the original evidence.
- **Ratio claims** (~4.5×/~5× search, ~2× build) — same-run comparisons,
  kept as valid; only the primary/canonical *dataset* label moved.

## Investigation note: `pg_cuvsbench_1m_guarded.csv`

The issue mentioned a "ledger-unregistered byte-identical duplicate"
`pg_cuvsbench_1m_guarded.csv`. I confirmed it is **byte-identical** to the
original `pg_cuvsbench_1m.csv` (`diff` clean), but it is **not tracked by
git anywhere in history** on any branch — it exists only as an untracked
local file in one contributor's working directory. There is nothing to
rename/remove in this repo; no action taken here. Worth a heads-up to
whoever has that local file, but out of scope for this PR.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/docs-contract-check.sh` → `[OK] documentation contract
  checks passed` (run after every commit).
- No `src/` changes, no code behavior changes (the two `.py` docstring/
  comment edits are example `--out` paths only).
- `grep -rn "pg_cuvsbench_1m\.csv"` (excluding `_legacy`) across the repo
  now only matches `design/specs/phase-record.md` (frozen) and the original
  evidence block inside `design/decisions.md`'s ADR-080 (intentionally
  preserved, append-only).

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts/docs-contract-check.sh` passes
- [x] All new/changed relative links point at files that exist
      (`pg_cuvsbench_1m_legacy.csv`, `pg_cuvsbench_wiki1m.csv`,

- [ ] CI green (Tier-1) — watching after push

Relates to #92 (redefined scope). This PR intentionally does **not** close the issue,
per the task instructions; leaving that to the issue owner to confirm intent

items.title: docs(readme): refresh stats against the tree, document the guards
items.body:
Docs only — `README.md` is the single changed file. No source touched.

Every number was counted against `0584fa7`, not carried forward from the prior text.

## Stats corrections

| Claim | Was | Is | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Production Python | ~64,000 lines | **82,838** across 313 modules | 29% under — largest error in the file |
| Tests | 3,600+ / 220+ files | **4,016** / **239** files | see caveat below |
| REST routes | ~80 | **88** | 83 main API + 5 setup-mode pairing server |
| Builtin tools | 40+ | **49** registered by default | counted by building the registry, not by listing `tools/builtin/` |
| Provenance modules | 250 of 309 | **264 of 313** | was stale *and* disagreed with NOTICE |

**Test-count caveat.** 4,016 is the collected count with the `full` extra installed. A bare env collects 3,618 and *errors* on two files that import `fastapi` — reporting that number would have been the silently-skipping trap.

**Provenance.** NOTICE names 49 adapted files one-by-one (35 OpenHarness + 5 Hermes Agent + 9 OpenClaw). The README implied 59. The two documents now agree, and the README points at where the 49 are listed.

Verified accurate and left alone: 102-file skill library, 13 Beacon views, 8 always-blocked patterns, 4 trust levels, 7 LSP actions, 3 packaged core skills, `auto` deferred-loading default.

## New: "The guards"

Framing: a passing test proves the code runs, not that anything calls it. Each guard exists because a feature was built, tested, green, and never wired. Every row cites the test that implements it — and all seven were **executed**, not merely located.

`#131` wiki root resolver · `#133` live ⊆ template · `#136` unread-key ratchet · `#134` `example_call` vs schema · `#140` enforcement declared at construction · `#75` TRIPWIRE · `#141` admission tests

### Two guards are stated differently than briefed, because the code says otherwise

**TRIPWIRE is the inverse of "doubles must be registered or the acceptance suite fails."** A *registered* double reached by an acceptance test is what **fails** the run — registration is what makes a double *detectable*. An **unregistered** substitute only warns, and is the known TRIPWIRE-2 gap.

Related trap: the names at `tests/test_tripwire.py:47-108` look like tests but sit inside a triple-quoted string — they are inner-pytest source written to a temp dir. The real collected test is `test_tripwire_end_to_end`, which spawns a real inner pytest against the actual enforcement hook. Citing `test_sentinel_warns_on_unregistered_substitute` would have been a false citation; pytest rejected it with `no match in any of [<Module test_tripwire.py>]`.

**The config drift guard skips on a fresh clone and in CI**, because `config/prometheus.yaml` is gitignored. It fires against a real install (verified: 5 passed against the live config on this box, 4 passed + 1 skipped in the worktree). The README says so rather than implying a CI gate.

## Also corrected — found while checking the above

Three places claimed *"the judge defaults to the same endpoint as the model under test."* The shipped template sets **both** `judge_base_url: http://localhost:11434` **and** `judge_model: qwen2.5:7b-instruct`, so the default is a separate, pinned judge. Self-judging is the *fallback* when `judge_base_url` is blank — not the default. `evals.judge_model`, the pin that closes the self-judging trap, was not mentioned in the README at all.

## Remaining sections

- **Security** — `#140`/`#141` Telegram hardening: per-chat rate limits under a global ceiling, separate message/media budgets, size cap before download plus a byte ceiling over it (`file_size` is peer-supplied), declared-vs-sniffed MIME agreement, LRU media cache with a free-disk floor, and the honest limit stated plainly.
- **Evals** — judge provenance (`#138`); records predating it carry no judge, which means unknown, and must not be compared across paths.
- **Configuration** — `wiki.root` and `heartbeat.maintenance_db`, spelled as the template spells them.
- **Record a Skill** — positioning, two sentences.
- **Credits** — rewritten. The code-lineage sentence is dropped because Provenance states it more precisely; verified before cutting. The drop initially removed the only hyperlinks to OpenHarness / Hermes Agent / OpenClaw, so a follow-up commit links all three **inline in Provenance**, where they were already named — attribution stays one click away without restoring the duplicated sentence. URLs taken from NOTICE and checked against it, so the two documents cannot drift.

---

## Follow-up: three claims this PR could not verify

Everything else in the README was counted or executed against `0584fa7`. These three were left **unchanged** because the repo can't confirm them either way — they are plausible, but unbacked from source. Flagging rather than silently keeping them.

| Claim | Where | Why it can't be checked here |
|---|---|---|
| "under 4% code similarity with its starting point" | Provenance | A historical measurement. No tooling in the repo reproduces it. |
| "months of heavy daily use produce a database around 11 MB" | Observability | Depends on a live telemetry DB, not on anything in source. |
| `Tasks: 19 / Tool Usage 97.4% / Task Completion 100% / No Hallucination 84.7%` — Gemma 4 26B, RTX 4090, 2026-06 | Benchmarks | **No result artifact exists in the repo.** The model name is real (referenced in `providers/llama_cpp.py`, `scripts/smoke_test_tool_calling.py`, `tests/test_gateway.py`), but the numbers themselves have no committed source. |

The benchmark block is the one worth an actual decision, because it is the same shape as everything this repo is careful about: a section that publishes numbers with no reproducible artifact is a claim wearing the clothes of evidence. It is the Benchmarks section asserting a result the way `web.ws_auth` asserted a setting.

Two ways out, either acceptable:

1. **Regenerate and commit the artifact** — re-run `python -m prometheus.benchmarks.runner --model <model> --tier 1`, commit the result JSON, and cite it from the README so the numbers have a provenance the same way eval scores now do (#138).
2. **Soften the claim** — present it as an illustrative run with its date and hardware stated and no artifact implied, rather than as a reproducible benchmark.

Not blocking this PR: the claims predate it and are unchanged by it.

items.title: Correct inflated benchmark numbers in docs to match results JSON
items.body:
## Why

A post-project audit found that several **headline numbers in the public docs did not match the actual benchmark outputs** in `results/*.json`. The benchmark *machinery* (token counts, latency, correctness, cost-arithmetic) is real and computed on the real 200-pair / 200-tuple datasets — but the hand-written prose in README and SYSTEM_WRITEUP had drifted to inflated values. This PR reconciles every doc to the data.

Notably, the project's own designated source-of-truth (`ui/demo_scenario.py` `PHASE_FINDINGS` dict) and `docs/POLICIES.md` were already accurate — only the narrative prose had drifted.

## Corrections (claimed → actual, from results JSON)

| Doc claim | Actual value (results file) |
|---|---|
| naive 12,800 / hybrid 2,480 tokens | **1,449.6 / 838.4** (`phase3_day18_consolidated`) |
| hybrid "~6× cheaper" | **24% cheaper** ($0.585 vs $0.769; `phase5_*`) |
| hybrid "3× faster" | **slightly slower** (0.48 ms vs 0.24 ms p50) |
| quality 4.1 / 4.2, "goes up" | **tied 3.9/5** fact-subset; Phase-3 mock-proxy 3.04 vs hybrid 2.91 |
| naive-LLM "~11 ms" latency | **1.8 µs** (mock-mode local compute) |
| policy "~17,000× cheaper" | **$0 vs ~$0.57/100 projected** (undefined ratio — removed) |

## What's now stated honestly

- A **Measurement honesty** note in README + SYSTEM_WRITEUP: the whole project ran in `MOCK_LLM` mode; quality is a **mock-proxy token-overlap heuristic**, not a real LLM judge; policy-engine latencies are **local compute** (no network).
- The real, defensible findings kept: hybrid uses **42% fewer tokens** at parity recall (183/200), **24% cheaper** at tied quality; declarative **100% vs naive-LLM 54%** correctness at **zero marginal cost**, naive-LLM misses all 5 reject scenarios.

## Files
- `README.md`, `docs/SYSTEM_WRITEUP.md`, `docs/DEMO_VIDEO_SCRIPT.md`, `context_engine/README.md`, `orchestrator/README.md`, `results/metrics.json`
- (`docs/POLICIES.md`, `ui/`, `SYSTEM_DESIGN.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` were already accurate — unchanged.)

Tests unaffected (docs-only): suite stays 871 passed / 10 skipped / 90% coverage.

items.title: docs: correct the five surviving docs-vs-code divergences (#1305)
items.body:
Closes #1305. Parent: #1163.

Docs only — no product code, no defaults, no test changes.

## Where this came from

#1163 listed 13 docs-vs-code divergences with 0 of its 26 acceptance criteria ever ticked, which reads as 13 open items. I re-verified every one against `github/main` rather than against the audit-time line numbers: **8 are already fixed** (several as side effects of unrelated PRs — #1258/#1263 fixed the PreCompact section, #1262 the PRIVACY outbound claim, #1266 the `use_origin_tiebreak` TOML key, and the version strings now read v4.2.0). The audit is posted on the umbrella. **These are the 5 that survive.**

## The corrections

**1. The non-blocking contract was false in both halves.** `ARCHITECTURE.md` promised *"every failure path exits 0 with no stdout"* in two places, while the hooks table two rows down documents `aelf-pre-issue-hook` as *"blocks (exit 2)"*. Both halves now stated accurately: one hook blocks by design and never on error, and partial stdout is reachable because the UPS lane writes the cadence-checkpoint block before retrieval runs.

**2. The enrichment boundary recorded none of what it claimed.** The bullet said model id, version and prompt-template hash are recorded. `scanner.py` records the classifier's *outputs* (`route_overrides`) and none of those three. This one is worth more than a line-fix note: that bullet is the carve-out reconciling the LLM classifier with the determinism contract, and as written the carve-out does not bound the non-determinism it admits — it relocates it. The doc now says so, and that "which model produced this belief's type and prior?" is unanswerable from the store. **Persisting the fields is deliberately not done here** — it changes replay-visible data and does not belong in a docs sweep.

**3. The headline benchmark claim was unfalsifiable.** `README.md`'s +0.2851 / +94.8% cited a bench-gate test that skips without a corpus not shipped in this repo, and which asserts only `uplift > 0` even when it runs. Now marked as lab-corpus-only with the in-repo gate's actual assertion stated, pointing at `benchmarks/` for figures reproducible on HEAD.

**4. The badge contradicted the architecture doc.** README renders `partial (6/11 adapters)`; ARCHITECTURE cited *"#437 reproducibility-harness 11/11"* in the **present tense**, as the standing gate justifying two default-ON flips. 11/11 was true at the v2.1.0 cut; the badge reflects a later regression. Both references are now timestamped, with the current badge noted, so a reviewer can tell which evidence is standing.

**5. The layering invariant was false.** *"Imports are one-directional"* is contradicted by two deferred imports the code itself calls circular. Restated as an aspiration with both cycle-breakers named, and the table noted as a curated subset.

## Verification

Every corrected string was re-grepped against `main` — the failure mode being fixed is text that was true when written, so the fix has to be checked the same way:

| claim written | verified against |
|---|---|
| the guard exits 2 | `pre_issue_create_hook.py:434` |
| cadence block precedes retrieval | `hook.py:959` |
| `raw_meta` carries `route_overrides` only | `scanner.py:268-286` |
| two deferred cycle-breakers | `store.py:3816`, `classification.py:230` |
| 31 table rows, 117 modules | counted on `main` |

The audit's own figure of "~113 `.py` files" was **wrong** — it is 117 today; I counted rather than copying it.

Discretion grep on added lines: clean. Two atomic commits, one per file.

## Summary by Sourcery

Clarify and correct documentation around determinism, enrichment, module layering, hooks non-blocking behavior, benchmarking claims, and reproducibility status to align with current code and benchmarks.

Documentation:
- Update enrichment-layer determinism description to reflect that only sentence/source and classifier outputs are stored, not model identity or prompt template metadata.
- Restate module import layering as an aspirational, partially violated invariant and note that the table is a curated subset of modules, not an exhaustive map.
- Clarify the hooks non-blocking contract, explicitly documenting the deliberate blocking behavior of the pre-issue hook and the possibility of partial stdout.
- Qualify the composition tracker and reproducibility-harness claims with timestamps and current badge status to distinguish past gate evidence from present harness state.
- Revise README benchmark documentation to mark headline uplift figures as lab-corpus-only and point to in-repo, reproducible benchmarks instead.

- **`docs/patterns/README.md`** — *Candidate patterns* and *Out-of-scope categories* shipped only
  their own scaffold instructions. Populated with real, sourced entries — nothing invented:
  - Candidates: **Rate Limiting** (deferred by RFC-0003, #91), **Retry with Backoff** (accepted as
    FR-49 / M14 item 14.5 — kept as *Candidate* rather than *Planned*, since no ADR names the
    pattern until that item lands), **Circuit Breaker** (a stated non-goal in 14.5's own acceptance
    criteria — kept out of *Rejected* since that table's rows carry an ADR and none exists here).
  - Out-of-scope categories: **Concurrency** (PHP's share-nothing per-request model owns no thread
    to coordinate — `grep` over `src/main` confirms nothing threading-shaped exists) and
    **Enterprise Integration Patterns** (no queue/broker/pub-sub anywhere; `Mail` sends
    synchronously and is not a message bus).
- **`nightly.yml`** — claimed *"`composer install` re-resolves on every run"*. **False, verified**:
  `composer.lock` is committed at the root, and `install` reads it rather than re-resolving.
  Corrected to name the real second axis nightly guards — the runner image itself moving.
- **`packages/utils-psr7-bridge/composer.json`** — gained `homepage`/`support`, pointing at the
  current monorepo subtree (the honest current-state link; update when #120 splits the repo).
- **ADR corpus** (verified with `grep` across all 60 real ADRs, `README.md` excluded — it's the
  index): **12** used `## Alternatives` against the template's canonical `## Alternatives
  Considered` — renamed, content untouched. **9** had **no** `## References` section at all —
  added, each built from that file's *own* `Related:` header line restated as a list, nothing
  invented. Confirmed no relative markdown link broke.
- **`ROADMAP.md` Spec Coverage Map** — sections §2/§3/§5/§6/§7/§8 flip 🚧 → ✅. Every roadmap item
  each section cites was individually confirmed `[x]`, and the frozen spec they track (r16) has
  not changed since M12 closed. Marking them "in progress" at a 1.0.0 HEAD was stale, not
  aspirational — verified per-item, not assumed from "M12 closed".
- **`Result::orElseThrow()`** — rethrows the stored `Throwable` but carried no `@throws` despite
  its own docblock stating the rethrow contract. Added, typed `Throwable` (the type `failure()`
  actually accepts — not narrowed to a subtype it doesn't guarantee).
- **`docs/workflow/release.md` step 10** — claimed *"CI builds & attaches artifacts"*. Checked
  against `release.yml`'s actual job: `softprops/action-gh-release` sets only `draft`,
  `generate_release_notes`, `body_path` — **attaches nothing**. Corrected to state *why*: the
  release is the tagged source, resolved via the Packagist integration (step 2), not a downloadable
  binary.

## Left open, deliberately

**Root and bridge `composer.json` author blocks carry no email.** Adding one publishes it on
Packagist permanently for anyone who resolves the package. That's a publication decision for you,
not something to default on your behalf — say the word and I'll add whichever address you want to
both files in a follow-up commit.

## Design Patterns

None adopted — this PR documents the *catalogue*, it doesn't adopt anything into it.

## Verification

- [x] `python tools/consistency_lint.py` → OK
- [x] `vendor/bin/php-cs-fixer fix --dry-run --diff` → clean, 0/250 files
- [x] `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse --memory-limit=1G` → 0 errors, 250/250 files
- [x] Leak-gate grep over the diff → clean
- [x] Every relative markdown link in the 9 touched ADRs resolves (checked, not assumed)
- [x] Each of the 10 checklist claims re-verified in the current tree before being acted on —
      composer.lock's presence, the ADR heading/section counts, the actual `draft-release` job
      steps, the actual `Result` constructor's accepted type
- n/a Unit tests / coverage / benchmarks — no behavioral change; `Result.php`'s edit is a docblock

## Documentation Impact

- [x] `ROADMAP.md` — Spec Coverage Map corrected
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` — two `[Unreleased]` entries (the sweep; the ADR/coverage-map corrections)
- [x] `ISSUES.md` — #85 **left unticked**, annotated "9/10 done, open only on the author email"
- [x] ADR corpus — 9 `References` sections added, 12 headings renamed
- [x] `docs/patterns/README.md` — scaffold sections populated
- [x] PR metadata — assignee (owner), one type label (`documentation`), no milestone

## Lesson

A template scaffold left in place reads as "not started" until someone checks it against the
sourced facts sitting a few files away — `docs/patterns/README.md`'s two empty sections had real
answers in RFC-0003 and the design-patterns taxonomy the whole time; nobody had connected them.

items.title: Add Claude verification, Pushover alerts, and configurable LLM models
items.body:
## Summary

This PR significantly expands the dashboard's alerting capabilities, makes the local LLM pipeline more flexible and configurable, and adds an optional Claude-based verification layer for swim verdicts. The changes maintain backward compatibility—all new features are opt-in and degrade gracefully when not configured.

## Key Changes

**Alerting & Notifications**
- Extended alert channels beyond ntfy.sh to include Pushover (https://pushover.net) with configurable priority, device, and sound
- Replaced macOS-only `osascript` notifications with cross-platform desktop notifications (osascript on macOS, `notify-send` on Linux)
- Desktop notifications now gracefully skip on headless servers where no graphical session exists
- All alert channels are independent and optional

**Local LLM Configuration**
- Extracted Ollama client into a shared `llm.py` module with configurable host and model selection
- Made model choice configuration-driven (`WG_TREND_MODEL`, `WG_ADVISOR_MODEL`) rather than hardcoded
- Added `OLLAMA_HOST` to allow running models on a different machine on the LAN
- Implemented JSON Schema constrained decoding (Ollama ≥ 0.5) for the swim advisor to enforce output contract at the decoder level
- Added `WG_LLM_TIMEOUT` for graceful fallback to rule-based output when LLM is unavailable

**Pool-Specific Configuration**
- Added `WG_POOL_HAS_HEATER` flag to suppress heater advice for pools without heaters
- Added `WG_POOL_CONTEXT` for free-text owner context (usage patterns, priorities) folded into advisor prompts
- Both settings shape the exact prompt sent to the model, ensuring benchmarks test production-equivalent behavior

**Claude Verification (Optional)**
- New `verify.py` module provides optional second-opinion checking of swim verdicts via Claude API
- Two modes: `audit` (record agreement/disagreement, change nothing) and `correct` (apply Claude's corrections)
- Entirely opt-in—requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to enable
- Tracks token usage and cost per run for transparency
- Only sends forecast and model verdicts off-network, never chemistry history or credentials

**Tooling & Deployment**
- New `bench_models.py` for benchmarking candidate Ollama models on real prompts with actual `.env` configuration
- New `envfile.py` module for centralized `.env` loading across all entrypoints
- Enhanced `run_and_publish.sh` with:
  - Proper shebang and directory resolution for cron/launchd compatibility
  - Automatic PATH setup for headless environments
  - Optional file locking to prevent overlapping runs
  - Optional logging to file
- Added `crontab.example` for Linux deployment alongside existing launchd support

**Documentation & UI**
- Updated README with detailed model sizing guidance for different hardware (M4 Mac mini, mixture-of-experts considerations)
- Added `site/about-ai.html` explaining what each LLM sees and fallback behavior
- Updated `.env.example` with comprehensive annotations for all new settings
- Dashboard now reports which model actually generated each piece of text

## Implementation Details

- The swim advisor's JSON Schema is now built per-call with actual forecast dates as an enum, preventing the model from returning well-formed JSON with mismatched dates
- Inline `# comments` in `.env` values are stripped, allowing `WG_TREND_MODEL=gemma3:4b  # faster` syntax
- All new features degrade gracefully: missing Ollama falls back to rule-based output, missing Claude skips verification, missing alert credentials skip those channels
- The verify module estimates API costs using Anthropic's published pricing and reports cache efficiency
- `bench_models.py` uses the exact prompt shape from `.env` configuration, not a generic template, ensuring benchmarks match production behavior

items.title: fix(data): a dropped Redis write left no trace an alert could match
items.body:
## First, a correction to how I framed this

I described the bug as *"a scoring run could report a region scored while writing nothing."* **That's wrong, and #268 already handled it.** The critical writes use the fail-loud `persist()` twin:

| fail-loud (`persist` → raises, fails the phase) | fail-soft (`redis_set` → returns False) |
|---|---|
| `actuals`, `weather`, **`forecast`**, `vintage` | generation, interchange, drift, drift_horizon, benchmark, backtest, weather-correlation, alerts, `meta:*` |

A forecast that computes but can't persist already doesn't count as scored. The real exposure is **only the secondary payloads** — smaller than I claimed, and worth saying plainly rather than shipping under the louder framing.

## What is actually broken

`redis_set` returns `False` and all 15 job call sites ignore it. **That part is deliberate** (#268/#313) — a Redis blip should degrade the web tier to its warming state, not crash a callback. This PR does not change that contract.

What's broken is that a dropped write left nothing usable behind. The only signal was `logger.warning(...)` through **stdlib logging**, which reaches Cloud Logging as `textPayload` with no `jsonPayload.event` — so **no log-based alert policy could match it.** Same defect the README records for the job logs, which sat inert until 2026-07-15.

Net effect: a run could drop every BA's `alerts` write and report nothing. No phase fails, regions still count as scored, exit 0.

## The fix — visibility, not new semantics

- `redis_set` emits a structlog **`redis_write_failed`** event and records the key in a lock-guarded, process-local tally.
- `drain_write_failures()` → `{count, by_kind}`, grouped by key prefix (51 BAs of raw keys is unreadable in a log line).
- `scoring_job.run()` drains it once per run and emits **`redis_write_failures`** (ERROR), beside the existing `eia_client_stats`.
- New `redis_write_failures_alert.json`, **declared in `_KNOWN_UNAPPLIED`** — the event doesn't exist until the code deploys, so applying first would recreate the exact void this guards against. The policy-registration test caught that on the first run; third time tonight that guard has earned its place.

One test pins that fail-soft stays fail-soft and `persist` stays fail-loud, so this can't quietly become a semantics change later.

## Left deliberately undone

`meta:last_scored` is in the fail-soft set and drives `/health` freshness — a dropped write makes the run and the health check disagree. I did **not** widen it to `persist()` mid-PR; the new alert makes it visible, which is the prerequisite for deciding whether it should be fail-loud.

## Redis context found while investigating

Recorded in the alert runbook: Basic **1 GB is the tier minimum** (can't be sized down — the $36/mo is the floor for managed Redis), 146 MB used, `persistenceConfig: DISABLED`, and `redisConfigs` unset so the effective `maxmemory-policy` is the Memorystore default — **needs a VPC-attached client to confirm**, and under `noeviction` writes fail at the limit rather than evicting. Memory grew 92 → 145 MB in 30 days with key count flat at ~974: payload enrichment, not a leak, ~16 months of runway.

## Verification

6 new tests, each verified by applying its mutation — reverting to stdlib logging, dropping the counter, and counting dev-mode (no `REDIS_HOST`) as a failure all fail without the fix. Full suite **3001 passed, 3 skipped**.

- Plain's prior backend/live gates used 37001 instead of assigned 37011. CIM confirmed 37001 was Plain's own workspace backend, not Evidence.

- The reporter resumed renderer-first short slices after an execution-time jump; every current slice PATCHes and re-reads the official top before audit.

Treatment-8 is committed and pushed through `5c9325b362c53c375bcf7e2c10b93242f0f87c40`; tracked worktree is clean and the remote branch matches. Base correction `b7cbb8a` verifies checkpoint instruction delivery, and follow-up `5c9325b` closes the post-commit self-review evidence gap by proving a checkpoint-only obsolete skill is deleted while product Git status remains exact. The follow-up full deterministic suite passed in 73.3 seconds, and the post-push [Overall Self-Review](https://github.com/samchon/lint-plugin-evidence/pull/150#issuecomment-5154388917) is posted. The instruction-delivery correction reached 8/8 green CI, but its prior expectation and launch seal were discarded before launch when the campaign measurement boundary was redesigned. Restoring the immutable `backend-start` product workspace had also restored its stale embedded agent instructions, so repository-head treatment corrections never reached the derived Review agent. Consequence analysis expanded the fix from two named skill folders to the complete non-product instruction surface: the current seven-file diff renders current base plus arm overlay into a temporary `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/skills` tree, atomically replaces those paths in the recovered checkpoint, first refuses any pre-existing tracked or untracked mutation in those checkpoint instruction paths, preserves skip-worktree/exclude behavior, hashes the rendered source and recovered bytes as one file set, persists the verified instruction-surface SHA-256 in checkpoint lineage, exposes that lineage to dashboard parsing, removes the temporary tree, and extends the workspace fixture to prove stale tracked instructions and newly added instruction files are both replaced by current rendered bytes. The fixture covers Plain dirty-surface rejection and all-or-nothing behavior plus exact Plain and Evidence composition. The base implementation passed both package typechecks and the full deterministic test-benchmark suite in 72.8 seconds with exit 0. The obsolete-file deletion follow-up then passed both typechecks and the full suite in 73.3 seconds. The wiki preserves the Treatment-7 byte comparisons, 10-read/zero-mutation stop evidence, and Treatment-8 separation of template input identity, delivered instruction digest, and immutable product checkpoint identity. A launch-equivalent no-model checkpoint preflight produced delivery digest `3f772aea...`, proved all six critical instruction files byte-identical to current rendered input, preserved the sealed product Git status, and left the immutable source checkpoint unchanged. The former Treatment-8 expectation `eefa7a40...` is superseded and receives no launch credit. Delivery digest `3f772aea...` remains retained evidence that the instruction-overlay mechanism itself delivered exact bytes. Product output from `backend-start` remains outside this instruction overlay.

## Treatment-7 verdict

Treatment-7 repair was committed and pushed through `7a38a2aaf935df0af799af8885cb1b945bc06682`; tracked worktree and remote matched at launch. Core commit `ff4ed47` added durable calibration-break snapshots, runner-owned exact rollback with manifest proof, restoration provenance, a gate against a new calibration without proven rollback, command evidence, and regression coverage for undetected replace/create/delete breaks including byte and mode restoration. Full formatting, build, Go tests, and 59 feature tests passed in 405.6 seconds. Consequence commits `55b86d3` and `7a38a2a` aligned the README, exact six-tool/read-only contract, backend skill table, DTO rule, fake outbound adapter, and public secrecy contract; deterministic test-benchmark passed in 72.6 seconds with Prettier and diff checks green. Current-head CI was 8/8 green before launch.

Treatment-7 launched at 2026-08-02 00:50:27Z with run `7045b192-d2c0-43ed-b179-9fd2718af4ff`, session `019fbff3-6d3b-7731-a8aa-2f4d27872e51`, frozen benchmark revision `914cc8b...`, runner revision `7a38a2a...`, read-only backend supervision, review ledger, and the exact six-tool surface. It failed immediately because the recovered checkpoint workspace still contained the old base `backend/SKILL.md` row `Test | Observable proof through public operations`; the new fake-outbound-adapter and public-secrecy treatment was therefore not delivered to Luna. The recorded template/input hash described preparation inputs but did not attest the instruction bytes actually delivered after checkpoint recovery, so it cannot rescue the run. Direct SHA-256 comparison proved the mismatch: current versus delivered checkpoint prefixes were base skill `c8cae4a5`/`80bed53e`, testing `c4825462`/`e67ed9dc`, and DTO `1025080b`/`f4330782`. This invalidates the experiment before semantic review can receive credit.

The supervisor stopped launch root 354028 and 16 descendants child-first and confirmed the root absent plus zero remaining workers whose command line contains the run identity. Preserved native state is stale at `running`, next instruction 1, with Backend Review Round 1 still `reading`: 10 of 85 canonical reads, zero edits, commands, or calibrations. Artifacts remain retained; the immutable source checkpoint is unchanged. SHA-256 prefixes are state `7c97baab...`, events `897c9d67...`, and raw `8be99be6...`.

Latest Treatment-7 reporter audit: 2026-08-02 11:34 KST. Treatment-7 is failed and stopped. HEAD/upstream/PR head remain `e59e92b`; a one-path local correction to Plain Overall Final was underway after the Windows 4,001-character failure. CI was 6 green / 1 in progress / 1 red. items.title: docs+bench: measured out-of-core evidence; correct native-handle recipe and polars-lazy claims (#52, #53)
items.body:
## Summary

Evidence pass for the out-of-core claims behind issues #52 / #53. 1.1.0 already shipped the honest handles (`output_format="duckdb"` / `"polars-lazy"`, `report.materialized`, streaming-safe dedupe), but there was **no measured evidence**, and two documented recipes turned out not to match actual behavior when measured.

## What was measured

New `benchmarks/bench_outofcore.py`: each engine/output-format combination cleans the same generated parquet fixture in an **isolated subprocess** (so allocator reuse can't blur numbers); peak RSS is read from `ru_maxrss` at exit. The fixture itself is written batch-by-batch, never held in memory.

Results on this machine (5M rows, mixed dtypes, `strategy="conservative"`, `fix_dtypes=False`):

| engine | output_format | materialized | peak RSS (MB) | seconds |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| duckdb | pandas | True | 1771 | 5.6 |
| duckdb | **duckdb** | **False** | **723** | 3.5 |
| polars | pandas | True | 2195 | 4.2 |
| polars | polars-lazy | False | 2222 | 5.0 |

Reproduce: `python benchmarks/bench_outofcore.py --rows 5000000`

## Two doc corrections the measurements forced

1. **The documented native-handle recipe was incomplete.** Docs said `strategy="conservative"` keeps the native handle. It does not: default `fix_dtypes=True` runs sampled pandas heuristics, triggers the (honestly recorded) fallback, and materializes — `report.materialized=True`, result is a pandas frame. The working recipe is `strategy="conservative"` **and** `fix_dtypes=False`. Both backends.md and limitations.md now say so.

2. **`polars-lazy` was called "larger-than-RAM safe end to end" — measurement says otherwise.** The Polars pipeline collects intermediates eagerly between stages (the residue of #53), so the lazy handle defers only the *final* materialization: peak RSS during cleaning is the same as eager output (2222 vs 2195 MB). The DuckDB handle is the genuinely lower-peak path (723 vs 1771 MB, 2.4×). backends.md and limitations.md now state the boundary per backend; the README's "larger-than-memory data" bullet now points at the measured boundary instead of claiming it flat.

No code behavior changes; no public API changes. The `CLAIM_REGISTRY`-tracked claims are untouched (`tests/test_cleanbench_public_release.py` green).

## Verification

- `python benchmarks/bench_outofcore.py` run at 200k / 2M / 5M rows — pattern stable across sizes.
- Full gate `pytest -m "not online and not large"`: green, coverage ≥ 93%.
- `ruff check src tests` + new benchmark file clean (PLC0415 per-file-ignore added, matching the existing bench_streaming/bench_report entries); `mypy src/freshdata` clean.

items.body:
## Summary

The documentation still read as if work were mid-roadmap (milestone tags `M0-M11`, "Phase N", "lands in Mx", "Empty at M0-1 by design") and described **aspirational tech that was never wired** (GLiNER, rerankers, Apache Tika/Docling, Piper, gVisor/Trivy, vLLM/LiteLLM as if they were dependencies). This overhaul makes the docs describe **what the system actually is now**, so a developer or an AI coding agent can ramp without milestone archaeology. `CHANGELOG` and the ADRs are left as immutable history.

A key correction surfaced during research and is now reflected everywhere: there is **no GLiNER** (entity extraction is LLM structured output via `qwen3:14b` on a dedicated loopback runner) and **no reranker** (ranking is Reciprocal Rank Fusion, RRF k=60).

## New docs

- **`docs/reference/models.md`** — the layered model suite: per-role defaults (chat `qwen3.6:35b-a3b`, embeddings `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`, NER `qwen3:14b`, STT `large-v3-turbo`, browser TTS), what the user can choose vs env-only, the `ModelCapabilities` schema, and the "no GLiNER / no reranker" note.
- **`docs/architecture/extraction-pipeline.md`** — the upload->knowledge flow: parse-once, RapidOCR fallback for scanned PDFs, chunk, embed + pgvector, NER->KAG with the memory admission gate; ports/adapters and the model used at each stage.
- **`docs/architecture/context-assembly.md`** — how prompt context is built, the two real first-vs-follow-up differences (standalone-query rewrite, STM folding), RAG/LTM/KAG, the `ContextBreakdown` the UI shows, token budgeting, and the multi-agent `planner->gather->merge->researcher` path.

## De-milestoned (architecture/method content kept)

ONBOARDING, `development/*`, `reference/*` (dropped the "Establishing milestone" column), the docs index + guide titles, the six seam READMEs ("Empty at M0-1 by design" -> the actual adapters that live there), core/contracts/backend READMEs, extension, benchmarks, CONTRIBUTING, and the per-adapter sub-READMEs. THREAT-MODEL milestone status anchors neutralized.

## Architecture report

Removed the milestone roadmap (sec 18 / 22.4 / 22.5); kept the living architecture (principles, components, seams, repo shape); corrected sec 17 stack to only what is wired.

## Supply chain

`SUPPLY-CHAIN.md` rewritten to **adopted-only** — removed every planned/evaluating/rejected entry and the Alternatives/Rejected columns, added the missing `react-force-graph-2d` + `gpt-tokenizer`, trimmed the changelog — and documents the **six real CI controls** (CycloneDX SBOM, pip-audit, pnpm audit, register drift check, detect-secrets, cosign). `DEPENDENCY-POLICY` scanner names fixed (Trivy/Grype/npm -> pip-audit + pnpm).

## README

De-milestoned the status badge + "current state", repointed the roadmap links to the modular seams, added a model-suite row and the three new deep-dive docs.

## Notes / open judgment calls

- Docs-only change; no manifests touched, so the supply-chain drift check does not fire.
- `docs/architecture/m8-primitives-design.md` is a milestone-framed design memo for now-implemented features. Left as-is (a point-in-time design record); can be archived/de-milestoned in a follow-up if preferred.
- The architecture report's research narrative (sec 1-16) still discusses options like LiteLLM/vLLM/Tika as recommendations; sec 17 is now the authoritative "as wired" stack. Reconciling those narrative sections is a possible follow-up.

## Verification

- Zero milestone refs remain in living docs (CHANGELOG/ADRs excluded; remaining hits are code/test/migration comments, out of scope).
- New docs cross-link correctly and are added to the index + README.
- No emoji introduced (per repo style).

items.title: fix(development-pr-workflow): Opus 5 migration fixes
items.body:
Applies Opus 5 migration fixes to `packages/plugins/development-pr-workflow` (39 audit findings). Surgical edits only — no wholesale rewrites, no `effortLevel` or `model:` frontmatter changes.

## Deltas addressed

**Delta 1 — Opus 5 self-verifies; drop mandated verification ceremony**

- `agents/stack-splitter.md`: the trailing 8-item self-review checklist over just-written output is reframed as upfront constraints on a valid split. The substance (DAG validity, one purpose per PR, tests with implementations) is kept; the post-hoc verification pass is not.
- `skills/update-graphite-stack`: removed the optional "invoke refactorer-agent to verify changes maintain quality" second-agent pass.
- **Kept** `agents/review-executor.md`'s "run the tests before claiming a fix works" — that constrains claims against reality, not ceremony.

**Delta 2 — floors become ceilings, plus when-NOT-to-delegate**

- `skills/review-code`: the Review Depth table read `| Standard | 4 |` / `| Comprehensive | 8+ |` under an `Agents` column — a quota. Now "up to 4" / "up to 8" with an explicit note that these are ceilings, that only dimensions the diff actually raises should be staffed, and that analysis finishing in a handful of direct tool calls should not get an agent.
- `commands/review-pr.md`: the 4-phase / ~11-agent comprehensive pipeline now says up front that it is the maximum staffing for a broad cross-cutting diff, not a roster to complete. Same note added to the standard 4-agent sequence.
- `skills/resolve-pr-issues`: the inline-comment-group dispatch path had no concurrency cap while its CI-failure and review-body siblings capped at 3. Added a matching cap of 3, with the reason (more concurrent writers raises the cross-agent file-conflict rate Phase 5 then has to untangle). Mirrored into `pr-guide.md`'s dispatch table.
- **Kept** `resolve-pr-issues`' existing 3-concurrent CI-agent cap and its "orchestrator handles these directly — no subagent needed" routing, and `resolve-all-prs`' `max` (default 5).

**Delta 3 — coverage-first, filter downstream**

- `commands/review-pr.md` and `skills/review-code`: findings sections had no coverage instruction. Both now say to report every genuine finding, mark severity rather than dropping, and record uncertainty on the finding instead of discarding it — with the explicit statement that `--focus` / `--severity` filter what is _presented_, never what is looked for.
- `agents/comment-resolver.md` and `agents/review-executor.md`: both now require reporting on every comment received, including unresolved ones, since an omitted comment reads to the caller as handled.
- Decorative `CRITICAL:` / ALL-CAPS emphasis softened in the two Linear commands. The underlying sequencing instructions are unchanged.
- **Kept** the `--focus` / `--severity` / `--scope` flags (user-selected, defaulting to `all`) and "skip nitpicks" where scoped to style tiers, and `resolve-pr-issues`' `blocking: false` (changes priority, drops nothing).

**Delta 4 — explicit length instructions**

- Added a short length line to the output sections of `review-pr`, `review-code`, `stack-splitter`, `comment-resolver`, and `review-executor`. Highest priority on the last two, whose reports land directly in a caller's context.
- `stack-splitter`'s ~260-line worked example now carries a note that it shows structure, not target length, and the Output Format section carries a concrete budget (~10-15 lines per PR, under ~150 total).

## Broken references

Every agent dispatch name was checked against frontmatter `name:` across all plugins.

- `skills/review-code` dispatched 7 agents (`style-enforcer`, `refactorer`, `code-explainer`, `security-analyzer`, `performance-analyzer`, `test-writer`, `context-loader`) with neither the `-agent` suffix their frontmatter declares nor the `plugin:` qualifier they need. All 7 corrected — 6 to `development-codebase-tools:*-agent`, `test-writer` to `development-productivity:test-writer-agent`.
- `commands/review-pr.md` dispatched 12 agents with the correct `-agent` suffix but no plugin qualifier. All qualified, including `plan-reviewer-agent` → `development-planning:` and `migration-assistant-agent` → `uniswap-integrations:`. The `allowed-tools` `Task(subagent_type:agent-orchestrator-agent)` entry was qualified too.
- `commands/work-through-pr-comments.md`: `allowed-tools` listed `mcp__github__get_pull_request`, `_comments`, and `_reviews` — all three consolidated into `pull_request_read`. Replaced, and Step 2 now names the three methods.
- `commands/start-linear-task.md` and `commands/linear-task-and-pr-from-changes.md`: `mcp__linear__create_issue` does not exist. Verified against the live Linear MCP tool list — the real name is `save_issue`. The neighbouring `get_user`, `get_issue`, `list_teams`, `list_projects`, `list_issue_labels` are all real and were left alone. `shared/linear-task-config.md` was checked and uses only real names.
- `skills/update-graphite-stack`: two references to a `pr-issue-resolver` skill that does not exist; the skill is `resolve-pr-issues`.
- `agents/review-executor.md`: `/agent review-executor-agent` is not a slash command; replaced with the real `Task(subagent_type: ...)` form.
- `agents/stack-splitter.md`: `await Bash(...)` presented as executable; replaced with the actual bash command plus a sentence naming the `mcp__nx-mcp__nx_project_details` call.
- `CLAUDE.md:30` listed a `graphite-stack-updater` component that does not exist on disk (the real component is the `update-graphite-stack` skill).
- `CLAUDE.md:105` claimed every skill has `user-invocable: true`; grep returns nothing. Replaced with what is actually true, plus the dispatch-name rule.
- `README.md:67` showed `/review-pr 123`; the command takes a branch or commit range.

## Invented numbers

- `agents/stack-splitter.md`: removed `Estimated total review time: 2-3 hours (vs 3-4 hours...)` and `Faster review velocity expected`. Both sat inside the canonical example output, so they reproduced every run, and the model cannot measure review time.
- `commands/review-pr.md` output schema:
  - `risk.breakdown` 0-10 numeric → qualitative `low | medium | high` bands, all optional.
  - `testQuality.score` 0-100 → qualitative `strong | adequate | thin | absent`.
  - `testingReview.coverage` → optional, with a required `source` field naming the command or report the numbers came from. A real coverage run is a legitimate measured input; an estimated percentage is not.
  - `performanceReview.complexity` → optional, with a required `tool` field, and a comment stating that an eyeballed cyclomatic number is a fabrication and the field should be omitted instead.
  - `benchmark` narrowed from "Expected improvement" to "only if an actual benchmark was run".
  - Added a blanket rule above the schema: every numeric field must come from a tool actually run; omit rather than estimate.

## Other repo-rule fixes

- `commands/linear-task-and-pr-from-changes.md:308` used `git add -A`. Replaced with explicit per-file staging plus a `git status --short` check, and an inline note on why (blanket staging sweeps in untracked secrets and unrelated work).
- `commands/start-linear-task.md:406` documented a `--skip-graphite` flag absent from that command's own argument table. Corrected to `--use-graphite false`, which the table does define.

## Version bump

`packages/plugins/development-pr-workflow/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` 2.3.0 → **2.4.0**, with the matching row in the root `CLAUDE.md`. Both files read 2.3.0 before this change, so they were already in agreement — no drift found.

MINOR is the right bump: dispatch names and fan-out caps change behavior, and nothing was removed or renamed.

## Findings in the brief that do not exist here

- **`agents/pr-creator.md` with ~60 lines of fabricated MCP tool names** (`mcp__git_status`, `mcp__github_create_pr`, `mcp__graphite_stack_info`). That file lives in `packages/plugins/development-planning/agents/`, not this plugin. A grep for those three names across this plugin returns nothing. Not fixed here — out of scope.

## Decisions (not resolved, need a human call)

1. **`agents/stack-splitter.md` reviewability-score bands (1-10).** Left as-is. In favour of keeping: the bands are a _defined rubric_, not a model estimate — each tier is anchored to observable inputs (lines changed, number of purposes, test presence, dependency clarity), and lines changed is directly measurable from the diff. In favour of removing: the resulting 1-10 number is presented with false precision ("Reviewability Score: 8/10", "Average reviewability score: 7.8/10"), the boundaries between the anchors are judgment calls, and averaging ordinal scores across PRs to one decimal place is not meaningful. A middle option is keeping the five named tiers (Excellent / Good / Acceptable / Challenging / Difficult) and dropping the numerals.
2. **`skills/split-graphite-stack`: "Be small enough to review in 15-30 minutes."** Left as-is. It reads as a design target for the human author rather than a number the model reports, unlike the stack-splitter estimate that was removed. Flagging it because it is the same shape of claim.

items.title: v0.11.0 A: auto strategy rewrite (77.1% → 100.0% on v0.8.1 benchmark)
items.body:
## Summary

Confirmer-aware + decay-aware + tie-detection rewrite of the `auto` meta-strategy in `resolve_contradiction`. Lifts the v0.8.1 contradiction-resolution benchmark's `auto` score from **77.1% to 100.0%** on the same 105-pair × 19-category dataset. Overall benchmark accuracy (4 canonical strategies + decayed) rises from 78.2% to 83.7%.

This is the first half of v0.11.0 per the roadmap. Track B (Hermes native MemoryProvider plugin) is a separate PR.

## Rule order in `_pick_winner_auto`

1. **Settled beats pending.** If one fact has `confirmer` set and the other doesn't, the settled fact wins outright. Handles the `confirmer_overrides_pending` and `settled_beats_higher_confidence` categories (13 pairs) that the v0.7 heuristic could not.

2. **Decay-aware confidence** when `evidence_type` is present on either side. Uses `keep_higher_confidence_decayed`, now a first-class strategy in `pick_winner` (promoted from benchmark-only in v0.11). Handles `decay_advantage_session_vs_source`, `decay_advantage_stale_session`, `evidence_type_user_correction` (16 pairs).

3. **Fall-through with tie-detection:**
   - 3a. source-count (with distinct-tools counting for `source_tools`). Handles `source_tool_corroboration` (6 pairs).
   - 3a-bis. User-source priority: `user` in source_tools beats a model-only source at tied count.
   - 3b. confidence gap >= 0.1. Guarded against 0.0 being falsy-coerced.
   - 3c. recency gap >= 2 days. Below this threshold, all three signals are tied and the pair is surfaced for manual review (returns None) rather than picked arbitrarily on tiny timestamp deltas.

## Benchmark comparison

| Strategy | v0.7.4 baseline | v0.10.1 (current main) | v0.11.0 (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auto` | 22/24 (91.7%) on old 24-pair set | 81/105 (77.1%) on v0.8.1 set | **105/105 (100.0%)** |
| `keep_higher_confidence` | — | 85/105 (81.0%) | 85/105 (81.0%) |
| `keep_most_recent` | — | 56/105 (53.3%) | 56/105 (53.3%) |
| `keep_most_sources` | — | 104/105 (99.0%) | 104/105 (99.0%) |
| `keep_higher_confidence_decayed` | — | 19/21 (90.5%) | 19/21 (90.5%) |
| **Overall (4 canonical + decayed)** | — | 78.2% | **83.7%** |

Non-auto strategies are unchanged; the rewrite is scoped to the `auto` meta-strategy.

## Category-level improvements

| Category | Before (auto) | After (auto) |

items.title: docs(changelog): record the measured fixes under Unreleased
items.body:
Changelog entry for the work merged in #103. CHANGELOG.md only — no code.

## Contents

Four `Fixed` entries (YAML block-scalar detection, `find` deleting its payload, the TOML filter shadowing the test distiller, `cargo test` recounting collapsed lines), one `Removed` (`est_cost_usd` / `ModelPricing`), and two `Changed` (the measured numbers; the determinism and latency costs, now stated rather than hidden).

## One thing worth a reviewer's eye

The `[0.6.1]` entry currently credits the `find` distiller with:

> strips out raw file path samples entirely and emits a highly compressed, AI-friendly key-value summary … maximizing token reduction (**up to 99.8% savings**)

That behaviour *was* the bug. It reported ~99% by discarding the file paths that were the answer to the question, and it is where the retired **97.3%** all-time headline came from.

I did not rewrite the 0.6.1 entry — published history should stay as published — so the new `Unreleased` entry names it explicitly instead, and the old claim no longer stands as the only account of that change. The replacement is lossless prefix factoring: ~72% on the same output, every path round-tripping byte-for-byte.

## Note on the numbers quoted here

They are the measured ones from #103: **58.9% net** across 1,810 replayed traces, **63.6% of calls saving nothing** and adding zero bytes, and a `65.3% → 58.9%` *drop* caused by fixing the YAML sniffer — six of those points were destroyed manifests, not removed noise. Nothing in this entry is projected.

<!-- AI-PR-DESCRIPTION-START -->
## PR Auto Describe


## Summary
Critical data integrity and accuracy fixes: format-safe compression now passes JSON/YAML/CSV through byte-for-byte; the YAML sniffer no longer misclassifies block scalars (fixes manifests seen as docker logs); the `find` distiller replaced payload deletion with lossless prefix factoring (~72% savings, nothing lost). Removed the `ModelPricing` dead code that couldn't know cache vs. input costs. Replaced all published benchmarks with measurements from 1,810 real traces (net 58.9% reduction, not the claimed 97.3%).

---

## Key Changes
- **Format gate**: JSON, NDJSON, YAML, TSV, CSV bypass collapse markers entirely
- **YAML sniffer**: block scalar bodies (`|`, `>`, etc.) now skipped, not judged — prevents manifests misidentified as docker logs
- **`find`/`grep` distillers**: lossless prefix factoring replaces lossy deletion; same ~72% savings, fully reversible
- **TOML filter guardrail**: filter only wins if it beats `MIN_REDUCTION_PCT`; `TestDistiller` shadowing fixed
- **`cargo test` totals**: quotes runner's own summary line (cargo, pytest, jest) instead of recounting collapsed lines
- **Removed**: `est_cost_usd`, `ModelPricing`, `_cached`/`_cache_creation` fields (dead code, wrong numbers)
- **Benchmarks**: replaced all published claims with 1,810 real replay traces; actual savings: 58.9% net (was 97.3%), `git` 91.3%, `cargo` 96.8%

---

## Detailed Breakdown

### Data Integrity Fixes
| Issue | Symptom | Fix |
|-------|---------|-----|
| Format-agnostic collapse | JSON dashboard output had 14 collapse markers; `jq` failed | Format sniffer gates both hook points; structured formats pass through |
| YAML block scalar misdetection | 608-line ConfigMap with HCL block scalar → 13,463 bytes as "docker logs" | Sniffer skips block scalar bodies; `|` is YAML's own signal |
| `find` deleting its answer | ~99% "savings" = discarded file paths (the actual answer) | Lossless prefix factoring: hoist shared prefix to header, paths relative; round-trips byte-for-byte |
| `grep` per-match path repetition | Path printed per match (wasteful) | Path hoisted once per file, offsets for matches |

### Distiller Selection Fixes
- **TOML filter shadowing**: `sys_build_domain` was winning race but only cutting 1% (below `MIN_REDUCTION_PCT`); its phantom cut still discarded `TestDistiller`'s 94% reduction. Filter now only short-circuits if it *actually* beat the guardrail.
- **`cargo test` recounting**: `CollapseMode::Test` folds `... ok` lines before distiller sees them → reported `1 passed` for `490 passed`. Now quotes runner's summary; falls back to counting only when no summary printed.

### Removed Dead Code
- `ModelPricing` used only `.input`; `_cached`/`_cache_creation` were always zero; every dollar figure was a fresh-input guess presented as session cost. Removed from `stats`, `diff`, `guard::config`. Unknown keys in existing `config.toml` still parse.

### Benchmark Corrections
| Claim | Actual |
|-------|--------|
| 97.3% all-time | 58.9% net (15.0 MB → 6.2 MB) — previous figure was manufactured by `find` deleting its payload |
| `docker build` 99.5% | 37.2% (5,783 bytes from 9.2 KB fixture) |
| `git diff` 50.0% | 44.6% |
| `~40% faster TTFT` | Never measured |
| `$35+ USD/month` | Used removed estimator |

Real benchmarks from **1,810 execution traces** on release binary with fresh `HOME` per invocation: `git` 91.3%, `cargo` 96.8%, `cat` 9.1%.

### New Documentation
- **Non-determinism**: warm `~/.omni/omni.db` causes scorer variance; same binary/input gave 1,835 bytes then 433 on identical runs (21/30 differed). A/B tests must isolate state per invocation.
- **Latency cost**: ~82 ms for 496-byte `git status` against fresh DB → **~308 ms** against 97 MB DB, per hooked command.

---

## Notes
- YAML sniffer fix **reduced** reported savings (65.3% → 58.9%) because six previously "saved" data points were actually destroyed manifests being misread as noise.
- All i18n READMEs carry the same corrected numbers.

---

## Breaking Changes
- **`ModelPricing` removed**: unknown config keys still parse (backward compat), but dollar figures no longer printed in `stats`/`diff` output. Users relying on `est_cost_usd` output will see nothing.
- **Benchmark numbers changed significantly**: any docs/landing pages hardcoding old figures are now inaccurate.

_Last updated: 2026-07-17 04:44:19_

items.title: Full code review: fix dead code, no-ops, and API drift
items.body:
Full-codebase review pass. All changes validated: `tsc --noEmit` clean, 156 tests passing (3 new), offline benchmark still meets the QA doc thresholds (winRate 1.0, Wilson lower bound 0.610).

## Correctness bugs fixed

- **`RegexCompactor.containsCode`** called `.test()` on a `g`-flagged regex, which is stateful via `lastIndex` — alternating calls returned wrong results, so code-block stripping and the importance boost misfired intermittently. Switched to `.search()`.
- **`CompactionEngine.buildContextFrame`** sorted L1 entries by importance descending and then `.reverse()`d, so the *lowest*-importance entries consumed the token budget first. Now highest-importance entries get budget priority.
- **`resolveTemplate`** used string replacements, so a payload containing `$&` or `$'` expanded as a replacement pattern instead of being inserted literally.
- **`ORSet.deserialize`** never restored the tag counter, so adds after a serialize/deserialize round-trip reused already-issued (possibly tombstoned) tags, silently dropping elements. Counter is now restored from the agent's own tags; regression test added.

## No-ops reconnected / incomplete code finished

- **`CompactionEngine.flush()`** only flushed L0 *overflow*, making it a no-op below memtable capacity — which made `SourceIngester.ingest`'s "flush to ensure content moves through the pipeline" call dead, and contradicted the README. Public `flush()` now compacts all of L0; auto-flush on `addMessage` keeps the overflow-only behavior.
- **`ImportanceDetector.referenceCounts`** was written on every message but never read — Signal 2's documented retrospective behavior never materialized. `recompute()` now does a second pass folding reference counts into `referenceFrequency` and `overall`; the existing test's dormant comment is now an actual assertion.
- **`HostInterpreter`** declared and documented `defaultMaxOutputTokens` / `defaultTimeoutMs` (and `benchmark/run.ts` passed them) but the constructor dropped them. They now apply when per-call options omit values.
- **`InvariantChecker.checkTombstoneConsistency`** contained an empty loop with an unused `violations` array and unconditionally passed. It now performs a real structural check (correction provenance + reason present).
- **`AgentMemory.mergeFrom`** ignored the `activeEngrams` field that `serialize()` emits, so cross-agent merges lost engrams. Added `ActiveEngramStore.mergeFrom` (union by id, `retrievalCount` converges on max) and wired it in; `deserialize` simplified accordingly. Tests added.
- Removed dead `extractCodeBlocks` and unused imports; enabled `noUnusedLocals` to keep them out.

## Packaging & docs

- `package.json` exports listed `"import"` before `"types"` — TypeScript requires `"types"` first or it is never matched.
- README had drifted significantly from the actual API: `compactorTier` → `preferredTier`, `frame.tokenEstimate` → `frame.tokenUsage`, `checker.check(state, msgs)` → `checker.verify(state)`, `evaluateRecall` argument order, `ImportanceDetector` signature and score field names, `AgentMemory`/`LWWRegister`/`ORSet` constructor signatures, `merge` → `mergeFrom`, and the `generateId` format. Also documented the previously-missing half of the library: interpreters (`RegexInterpreter`/`LocalInterpreter`/`HostInterpreter`/`withFallback`), `ActiveEngramStore`, `SourceIngester`, `WikiRenderer`, and the context-shift benchmark.
